headline: NVDA added 33.6% in a session and high-yield still widened 24bp — the squeeze repaired price, not plumbing.
summary: The violence reversed direction. S&P 500 +4.9% to 7,247, Nasdaq 100 +6.9% to 26,750, SMH +15.1%, SOXX +13.2%, NVDA +33.6% to 167.73, MU +18.8%, TSM +15.6%, ASML +9.7%, EWT +20.2% and EWY +10.5% as the offshore mirror caught up to a US session Asia never saw (TWII closed Friday -6.2%, KOSPI -5.2%, N225 -5.1%). Volatility broke: VIX -23.6% to 27.41, VIX3M -17.6% to 25.50. ARKK +8.9%, IPO +9.8%, SPHB +9.6%, MSTR +12.5%, COIN +8.4%. That is a short-cover and gamma-unwind rally in precisely the names that were margin-called, not a change in the macro.

Three tells say don't chase it. First, credit. The latest prints (20 Nov) have HY OAS +24bp on the day to 3.76, CCC +41bp to 14.02 (+95bp on the month, +365bp on three), BBB 1.22 and IG 0.98 — all four sitting at the 100th percentile of the 52-week range with 1m z-scores of 1.1 to 1.6. Equities retraced; spreads did not. Second, the dollar. DXY +0.5% to 104.36, 100th percentile, z=1.21 with acceleration +0.68; USDCAD +2.6% on the month (z=1.49, acc 1.16), USDBRL +18.1% (z=5.03, acc 3.95), USDKRW +0.6% with acceleration 0.91, CEW -2.3%. A genuine risk-on day does not come with the funding currency still accelerating higher. Third, the term structure: VIX/VIX3M fell 7.3% but is still 1.0749 — backwardated, 79th percentile. Hedges were trimmed, not retired. Risk regime improved all of two points, -23 to -21; credit & vol is still -57 and dollar -57.

What changed versus Friday is the shape, and it flipped completely. Friday's tape was differentiated — equal-weight beating the index, software beating silicon. Today it inverted: RSP/SPY -2.3%, IWM/SPY -1.8%, KRE/SPY -3.4%, XRT/SPY -3.5%, while QQQ/SPY +2.1%, SMH/SPY +9.9% and high-beta/low-vol +9.0% in a single session. IGV/SMH gave back 10.1% of its 17% monthly gain. In other words, the market bought back exactly the leverage it had just liquidated, and did it on narrowing breadth. The monthly damage is intact underneath: SMH -12.6%, MTUM -11.7% (z=-2.14), NVDA -20.5%, BTC -22.5% at 62,614, IBIT -22.9%, MSTR -40.1%, CAT -20.2% (z=-2.29), UNH -21.6%.

The real macro story is still a disinflation impulse colliding with an expensive front end. Brent -6.8% today to 86.26 and -26.1% on the month, WTI 80.02 (-22.5%), gasoline -25.2%, DBC 1m z=-2.98 — and 10-year breakevens at 2.15, the 0th percentile, with 5-year at 2.18. Yet the 3-month bill is 4.34% against an effective funds rate of 3.88%: 46bp of tightening priced into the next quarter, 3m10y flattened another 10bp to 60bp (1m z=-1.00), and the 10-year real yield is 2.88%, 94th percentile and 27% above its 200-day. That is passive tightening into falling nominal growth, with core CPI turning up (+30bp, z=0.93) and the inflation composite at 61. The clean beneficiaries are visible: India is the standout (BSESN +12.7% on the month, z=3.01, INDA +12.0%, rel. strength +18.5%) as an oil importer with USDINR -1.9%, while Brazil is the casualty (BVSP -19.4%, z=-3.66; EWZ -31.6%). Precious metals finally bounced out of forced-liquidation mode — gold +4.4%, silver +5.6%, GDX +7.4%, GDXJ +7.9%, gold/silver -1.2% off the 98th percentile. Own the dispersion and the disinflation; let someone else own the beta.

good.text: Historic upside squeeze in the exact names that were liquidated: SPX +4.9% to 7,247, NDX +6.9%, SMH +15.1%, SOXX +13.2%, NVDA +33.6%, MU +18.8%, TSM +15.6%, EWT +20.2%.
Volatility deflated hard: VIX -23.6% to 27.41 from Friday's 35.89, VIX3M -17.6% to 25.50, and the VIX/VIX3M ratio off 7.3% to 1.0749 — still backwardated but no longer deepening.
The disinflation rebate got bigger: Brent -6.8% to 86.26 (-26.1% on the month), WTI 80.02, gasoline -25.2%, broad commodities 1m z=-2.98, 10y breakevens 2.15 at the 0th percentile.
The precious-metals forced-sale signature is unwinding: gold +4.4% to 3,669, silver +5.6%, platinum +2.9%, GDX +7.4%, GDXJ +7.9%, gold/silver -1.2% from the 98th percentile.
India keeps compounding while the rest of EM bleeds: Sensex +12.7% on the month (z=3.01, acc 2.60), INDA +12.0% with +18.5% relative strength, USDINR -1.9%.
Cash-flow consumer names are still making highs on the real-income rebate: TGT +10.2% on the month, MCD +10.7%, COST +9.2%, HD +8.3%, WMT +7.1%, UPS +8.5%, with XLY turning up (+3.6%).

bad.text: Credit refused to confirm: HY OAS +24bp to 3.76 (+49bp on the month, z=1.63), CCC +41bp to 14.02, BBB 1.22, IG 0.98 — all four at the 100th percentile of the year.
The rally was narrow and leverage-led, not broad: RSP/SPY -2.3%, IWM/SPY -1.8%, KRE/SPY -3.4%, XRT/SPY -3.5% while high-beta/low-vol ripped +9.0% and SMH/SPY +9.9%.

Dollar squeeze is still accelerating through the risk rally: DXY +0.5% to 104.36 at the 100th percentile (acc z=0.68), USDCAD acc 1.16, USDBRL +18.1% on the month (z=5.03, acc 3.95), USDKRW acc 0.91, EM FX basket -2.3%.

The price of money keeps tightening passively: 3m bill 4.34% against 3.88% effective funds, 3m10y -10bp today to 60bp (1m z=-1.00), 10y real yield 2.88% at the 94th percentile and 27% above its 200-day.
Energy equities are accelerating lower, not basing: XLE acceleration z=-2.13, XOM -2.36, CVX -2.14, XOP -17.3% on the month with -13.1% relative strength, OIH -14.8%.
The LatAm and crypto stress blocks are untouched by today's bid: BVSP -19.4% on the month (z=-3.66), EWZ -31.6%, ARGT -23.1%, BTC -22.5%, ETH -25.1%, MSTR -40.1%, COIN -32.8%.

trades.name: Short credit beta vs duration
trades.line: Short HYG, long IEF: spreads at 100th pctile ignored the rip
trades.expr: Short HYG $1 against long IEF $1, equal dollars. Alternative via CDX HY payer or buying Dec/Jan HYG 74 puts financed by selling 79 calls.
trades.thesis: Equities retraced a week of losses in one session but every spread measure is at the 100th percentile of the year and still widening. Either credit catches up to the equity bid or equities roll back over; the pair pays in the second case and loses very little in the first because IEF is pinned by collapsing breakevens.
trades.trigger: HY OAS +24bp on the day to 3.76 and +49bp on the month (z=1.63), CCC +41bp to 14.02, BBB 1.22, IG 0.98 — all 100th percentile — while SPX printed +4.9%. HYG/IEF is still rolling over with a 1m z of -0.77.
trades.stop: HY OAS back under 3.35 and HYG/IEF reclaiming its 200-day (currently -0.45%); that means credit has ratified the equity rally.
trades.target: HY OAS 4.25-4.50, CCC through 15; pair up 3%.

trades.name: Fade the beta squeeze
trades.line: Short SPHB vs long SPLV after a +9.0% one-day beta rip
trades.expr: Short SPHB $1 vs long SPLV $1. Cleaner than an outright index short with VIX already down 23.6% in a day.
trades.thesis: High-beta/low-vol rose 9.0% in one session but is still -7.8% on the month with a rolling-over trend and a 1m z of -1.27. Short-covering rallies in the highest-beta decile do not fix funding; with VIX/VIX3M still backwardated at 1.0749 and spreads at the widest of the year, beta gives it back.
trades.trigger: SPHB +9.6% today, SPHB/SPLV +9.0%, RSP/SPY -2.3% and IWM/SPY -1.8% — the rally narrowed while beta exploded. MOVE still 104.45, +41.2% over three months.
trades.stop: VIX/VIX3M below 0.95 (contango restored) with SPHB/SPLV back above its 200-day; that is a genuine regime flip.
trades.target: SPHB/SPLV back toward the month's lows, pair +7%.

trades.name: Software over silicon, re-entry
trades.line: Long IGV vs short SMH after IGV/SMH gave back 10.1% in a day
trades.expr: Long IGV $1 vs short SMH $1. Scale the second half if IGV/SMH slips another 3%.
trades.thesis: The AI capex trade is still being repriced: SMH is -12.6% on the month, -8.2% relative to the S&P, and semis carry the capital-intensity and China/Taiwan risk. Software has the cash flow and the lower beta to memory pricing. Today's 15.1% semi squeeze handed back a third of the month's pair gain in one session — that is the entry.
trades.trigger: IGV/SMH -10.1% today versus +17% over the prior month; IGV trend turning up with its 1m z at -1.99 while SMH remains rolling over at the 37th percentile of its 52-week range.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH below 0.195, or SMH reclaiming its 200-day (currently -12.3% below).

trades.name: India over the EM complex
trades.line: Long INDA vs short EEM: oil importer wins, LatAm keeps bleeding
trades.expr: Long INDA $1 vs short EEM $1. Express directionally with INDA calls if you want convexity on the rupee.
trades.thesis: A 26% collapse in Brent is a direct terms-of-trade transfer to India, and it is already showing in both the index and the currency while the rest of EM is being hit by a 100th-percentile dollar and a Brazilian funding accident.
trades.trigger: Sensex +12.7% on the month at z=3.01 with acceleration 2.60, INDA +12.0% and +18.5% relative strength, USDINR -1.9% and rolling over; against EEM -6.4% on the month, EWZ -31.6%, BVSP z=-3.66, USDBRL z=5.03.
trades.stop: USDINR back above 95 or INDA relative strength turning negative on the month; also exit if Brent rallies back above 100.

trades.name: Gold miners off the liquidation low
trades.line: Long GDX: metals bounce says the forced selling is done
trades.expr: Long GDX outright; or long GDX / short GLD at 1:1 to isolate operating leverage. Jan 80 calls are the convex version.
trades.thesis: The November drawdown in gold and silver had the fingerprints of collateral liquidation, not a macro view — gold/silver at 84.7 in the 98th percentile, GDX down 29% in three months. With breakevens at the 0th percentile and the bills curve pricing tightening, the macro case is weak, but the flow case for a violent mean reversion off the 11th percentile is strong, and today confirmed it.
trades.trigger: Gold +4.4%, silver +5.6%, GDX +7.4%, GDXJ +7.9% on the day; GDX/gold acceleration z=+0.87 and gold/silver finally down 1.2% from its extreme.
trades.stop: Gold back below 3,450 or GDX giving back the whole of today's candle — then the liquidation wasn't finished.
trades.target: GDX 82 (+12%), back toward the 200-day it is 17.4% below.

trades.name: Crude crash: short producers, own the rebate
trades.line: Short XOP vs long XRT: the pump-price transfer is not priced
trades.expr: Short XOP $1 vs long XRT $1. For a lower-beta version, short XLE against long WMT/COST.
trades.thesis: Brent at 86 with gasoline -25% on the month is a direct hit to E&P cash flow and a direct subsidy to the consumer. The equity market has only partly marked the first leg and barely marked the second: XOP is still above the lows of its three-month relative range while retail's relative strength is turning up.
trades.trigger: Brent -6.8% today to 86.26 (1m z=-2.62, acceleration -2.58), WTI -4.7%, gasoline -25.2% on the month; XLE acceleration z=-2.13, XOM -2.36, CVX -2.14. On the other side XRT/SPY 1m z=1.02 and turning up, with WMT +7.1%, COST +9.2%, HD +8.3%, TGT +10.2%.
trades.stop: Brent back above 100, or XOP relative strength turning positive on the month.

trades.name: Sell the crypto-leverage bounce
trades.line: Short MSTR/COIN into a +12.5% dead-cat, BTC still -22.5% on month
trades.expr: Short MSTR 0.6 / COIN 0.4, or buy MSTR Jan 80 puts. Size small — these squeeze.
trades.thesis: Levered crypto proxies are the purest read on dollar funding, and funding has not improved: DXY at the 100th percentile, CCC spreads at 14.02, bills pricing hikes. MSTR bouncing 12.5% off a -40% month while bitcoin is still at the 11th percentile of its 52-week range is exit liquidity, not a bottom.
trades.trigger: MSTR +12.5% and COIN +8.4% today with BTC only +2.4% to 62,614 — the equity proxies out-rallied the asset by 4-5x on a day when HY spreads widened 24bp. IBIT -22.9% on the month, z=-1.71.
trades.stop: BTC back above 72,000, or HY OAS back inside 3.40 — the funding squeeze is over.
